what: Kernel #1 bandwidth pass 1: branchless FP4 decode + tile sweep
change_from_previous: The earlier kernel decoded FP4 by comparing each code against all 16 table entries and summing a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K, 16] tensor, a 16x expansion per load. Decode is now branchless from the code bits: magnitude from the low 3 bits, sign from bit 3, and E4M3 scales arithmetically since sm75 has no fp8 dtype.

verdict.achieved: 24.6 GB/s at N=1 on the best tile, up from 2.9 at the start.
verdict.target: 150 GB/s. So 16% of the stated target, 7.7% of hardware peak.
verdict.honest_position: This is real progress (8.5x on N=1 block time) and still far from the target. Bandwidth pass 1 is not the win Claude asked for, and the file says so.

what_is_still_wrong: Default tile (16/64/4 warps) is worse than the best tile by 3.6x, so the launch geometry matters more than the decode arithmetic at this size.

w13 and w2 behave differently: w2 stays flat to N=8 then degrades badly at 16/32, while w13 degrades steadily. Different contraction lengths (2304 vs 1152) mean different reuse; one schedule is unlikely to suit both.
24.6 GB/s on a 4KB-per-program tile is still launch- and latency-dominated. 2048 programs for w13 at BLOCK_N=64 across 8 experts is a lot of small work.
No CUDA graphs yet, no persistent-CTA variant, no vectorised 128-bit loads of the packed nibbles. Those were the levers Claude listed and only the decode was done.
next: Adopt the 64/32/2 tile as the default, add 128-bit vector loads and a persistent kernel, then re-sweep. Report again only when measured.
